title: Compact density token migration and accessibility compliance package for buttons, tables, charts
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Audit and remediate accessibility gaps introduced during the compact density token migration across buttons, table rows, and chart legends. Produce a compliance package (design spec, test cases, accessibility matrix, and handoff artifacts) suitable for stakeholder review and external accessibility validation. The work focuses on: 1) ensuring token color/contrast delta meets AA/AAA where feasible across light/dark themes, 2) clarifying ARIA roles and keyboard-focus order for dense tables and interactive chart legends, 3) improving touch target mapping and hit-box guidance for compact controls, and 4) adding SR announcements for pagination and dynamic table updates.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens documented with explicit contrast ratios and deltas for compact variants
Buttons and inline controls meet defined minimum touch target policy or have documented compensating controls
Dense table row focus order documented and verified with keyboard-only flows and screen reader narratives
Chart legend interactions have ARIA roles and keyboard navigation patterns defined; examples prototyped in Figma
Accessibility test matrix and checklist completed for all affected components (pass/fail per viewport and theme)
Compliance package (design spec + test cases + exportable accessibility matrix) uploaded to Confluence and linked in ticket
Engineering PRs referenced in this ticket include visual regression snapshots and axe/pa11y scan results
design_notes: We are migrating to the new compact token ramp (compact-shade-1..4). Early visual diffs show lowered contrast on outline buttons at small sizes; propose subtle elevation bump (0.5%) or retained stroke color for outline state in compact.
For chart legends, switch from role='img' to role='list' + role='listitem' for accessibility: this improves navigation for keyboard and voiceover when legends are interactive filters.
Table virtualization: announce row ranges in a single ARIA live region update (e.g., 'Rows 21–40 displayed') to avoid flooding screen readers when paginating rapidly.
Touch targets: in compact mode, keep visual touch size 32px but expand hit area to 44px via outline padding; document in token spec and component API (hitArea prop).
Provide example keyboard flows in Figma prototypes: focus rings, explicit tab stop ordering for compound cells, and alternative skip links for dense grids.
decisions: Keep compact color ramp but add targeted exceptions: outline buttons and disabled text will use a 'compact-contrast-boost' token to maintain >=4.5:1 where required.
Adopt list/listitem ARIA pattern for interactive legends to standardize across chart library wrappers (ChartJS wrapper + internal canvas components).
Use a single polite ARIA live region for table pagination and bulk updates to improve screen reader ergonomics.
Document hit-area expansion as the primary remediation for touch target regression rather than increasing visual density.
blockers: Engineering dependency: runtime theming patch needed to expose compact-contrast-boost token to Dedicated SDK (ENG-21288)
Design verification: need external screen reader session with a11y consultant to validate the proposed live region wording (scheduled but pending availability).
qa_plan: Run automated axe and pa11y scans across light/dark themes at small/medium/large viewport widths
Manual keyboard walkthroughs for header, table, and chart legend interactions on Win+NVDA and macOS+VoiceOver
Touch target verification on iOS/Android devices using device labs; confirm hit-area padding without visual regressions
Visual diffs for outline/button states in compact token set across planned themes
